a person who checks writing and fixes capitals, punctuation and spelling

cards.title: World Notes: Crowning a King or Queen
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: A coronation is the ceremony where a new king or queen is crowned. In England, it has been held in Westminster Abbey for hundreds of years.
Queen Victoria was crowned there in 1838, when she was 19. The crown was set on her head, and the people shouted, God save the Queen!
In Chapter 17, Aslan crowns the four children in the Great Hall of Cair Paravel, and everyone shouts, Long Live King Peter!

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. These are the last two chapters of the book. Watch how the ending answers the questions the beginning asked.
transcripts.guide1: Word work first: roots from the whole year, capital letters, and spelling patterns.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapters 16 and 17 with your lens. Then answer three questions.
transcripts.guide3: Today you add proof from the ending to your response.

notes.wordParts: Roots from this year: inter = between, trans = across, form = shape, ject = throw, script and scribe = write, port = carry, struct = build.
notes.grammar: An editor checks in passes. Capitals for names and the first word. Apostrophes for belonging and joined words. A comma before and or but when it joins two complete thoughts.
notes.spelling: Syllable types: closed (cat), open (go), silent-e (bake), vowel team (rain), r-controlled (car), consonant-le (table).
notes.wgrd: The ending answers the beginning. Edmund began as a traitor and ends as King Edmund the Just. The ending proves the theme.
vocab: the supreme ruler of a country or kingdom
the ceremony in which a ruler is officially crowned
restored to friendship or peace after a conflict

items.t: Peter tells Aslan that winning the battle was all Edmund’s doing.
items.why: He gives Edmund the credit he really earned.

items.t: Lucy is cross with Aslan, then says, “I’m sorry, Aslan,” and goes to help the others.
items.why: She owns up to being wrong right away.
